captures.description: NANOPUBLICATIONS, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: 'the smallest independent unit of publishable scientific information, represented as a machine-readable knowledge graph snippet rather than a traditional research paper.' The structure in three parts (assertion, provenance, publication info), four features (machine-readable in RDF and OWL, citable and attributed on a decentralized network, a life-sciences focus with 'millions' created, nanopub-py and the nanopublications site). Nine cards: nanopub.net, the nanopub-py repository, the retired Research Object page, IEEE Xplore, an NIH-hosted paper, Research Ideas and Outcomes, the Pensoft blog, the nanopub documentation, a Medium essay.

atoms.evidence: A nanopublication is the smallest independent unit of publishable scientific information
Every nanopublication is built using Resource Description Framework (RDF) triples and consists of three mandatory parts:
Citable and Attributed: Each nanopublication can be uniquely identified and tracked on a decentralized network, giving researchers credit for releasing granular data.
Publication Info: Metadata identifying the creator, creation timestamp, and reuse or licensing terms.
